title: Blackstone Lends $700M on Onni Group’s Luxury Rental Project
summary: Blackstone has provided a $700 million whole loan to the Onni Group for its newly completed luxury rental project in Seattle's South Lake Union neighborhood. The project, Onni South Lake Union, consists of 1,097 units across three buildings and 23,000 square feet of retail space, boasting resort-style amenities. This financing highlights continued capital availability for top sponsors even amidst market volatility, especially for projects in thriving life science and technology hubs like South Lake Union.

title: Newfold Digital completes MarkMonitor acquisition
summary: Newfold Digital has finalized its acquisition of MarkMonitor for $302.5 million from Clarivate Plc. MarkMonitor, a domain name registrar serving major brands like Amazon and Microsoft, will join Newfold Digital's portfolio, which includes Network Solutions and Register.com. This acquisition marks another instance of MarkMonitor changing private equity ownership, as Newfold Digital is backed by Clearlake Capital Group and Siris Capital Group.

title: Global Advisory Board to advise Deutsche Bank on key trends in business and politics
summary: Deutsche Bank's Management Board has established a new Global Advisory Board to provide advice on critical macroeconomic, geopolitical, and technological trends impacting the bank's operations. The board comprises prominent leaders from business, academia, and politics, including Paul Achleitner as Chairman, Henry Kissinger, and Eric Schmidt. This initiative aims to help Deutsche Bank navigate a rapidly changing global environment and better serve its clients.

title: Tech Moves: Athletic Greens hires Seattle tech vet Kelly Smith; Brex founder joins Expedia board
summary: Athletic Greens, a nutritional supplement company, has appointed Seattle tech veteran Kelly Smith as its chief digital officer. Smith brings extensive experience from companies like Hagerty, MGM Resorts International, and Starbucks, and has founded several startups. This article also highlights other significant personnel changes in the Pacific Northwest tech community, including new hires at Amazon Studios, Expedia Group, Microsoft's Xbox, CurvaFix, Nori, Flexport, and Bellevue College.

title: Meet NetApp BlueXP
summary: NetApp has introduced BlueXP, a unified control plane designed to simplify hybrid multicloud data services, addressing the challenges of managing data across diverse environments. BlueXP offers features for enhanced simplicity, security, cost savings through AIOps and flexible consumption, and sustainability by providing insights into energy consumption. It aims to empower organizations to innovate quickly while optimizing performance, cost, and security of their data infrastructure.

title: NetApp BlueXP is a big step towards true hybrid cloud data management
summary: NetApp has launched BlueXP, a new management and configuration offering designed to streamline hybrid cloud data management. BlueXP acts as a control plane, providing centralized visibility, AIOps-driven management, cyber resilience features, and governance for data spread across on-premises and public cloud environments. The service is free for all NetApp customers, reflecting years of NetApp's strategic focus on deep multi-cloud integrations.

title: Sonos Sub Mini Review: More Bass For Less Money
summary: The Sonos Sub Mini offers a more affordable and compact subwoofer option for existing Sonos owners, providing significant bass enhancement to home theater and whole-home audio setups. It features a unique cylindrical design, matte finish, and opposing dual woofers to reduce rumble, and integrates seamlessly with the Sonos app for setup and control. While it won't replace the larger Sonos Sub in terms of sheer volume, it's recommended for most users looking to boost their Sonos system, especially pairing well with the Sonos Beam (Gen 2).

title: Opinion | Elon Musk’s Biggest Problem on Twitter May Be Its Advertisers (Published 2022)
summary: Elon Musk's acquisition of Twitter poses a significant threat to the platform's advertising revenue, which is its primary source of income. Musk's actions, such as amplifying misinformation, have created concern among advertisers about brand safety and reputation. If advertisers flee en masse, it could financially cripple Twitter and endanger its future.

title: Amazon sell-off pushes market cap below $1 trillion for first time since April 2020
summary: Amazon's stock closed down for a fifth straight day, falling to its lowest point since April 2020, pushing its market capitalization below $1 trillion. This sell-off follows the company's disappointing fourth-quarter sales forecast and weaker-than-expected performance from Amazon Web Services. The e-retailer has been the second-worst performer in the Big Tech group this year, struggling like its peers with a slumping economy, inflation, and rising interest rates.

title: Dimensional US Sustainability Core 1 ETF Holdings
summary: This article details the Dimensional US Sustainability Core 1 ETF (DFSU) holdings as of its last reported update. The ETF, created on November 1, 2022, is an actively managed fund focusing on US equities across various market caps with high profitability and positive sustainability. It currently manages $2179.85 million in assets across 1907 holdings, with top investments including NVIDIA Corp, Apple Inc, and Amazon.com Inc.

title: Amazon Closes Below $1 Trillion in Market Value for First Time Since 2020
summary: Amazon's market value closed below $1 trillion for the first time since early 2020, with its shares falling 5.5% to $96.79. This decline is attributed to a weak forecast and broader tech industry slump, marking a 42% drop in the stock this year from its peak of nearly $1.9 trillion.

title: Peloton products now available at DICK'S Sporting Goods stores & online - get $100 gift card with purchase of Peloton Bike
summary: Peloton has officially launched its partnership with DICK'S Sporting Goods, making Peloton hardware and accessories available in select retail stores and online. Customers can purchase most Peloton hardware, excluding the Peloton Row, with pricing matching Peloton's website. A special promotion offers a $100 DICK'S gift card with the purchase of an original Peloton Bike for in-store self-assembly pickup.

title: Market Rallies Off Lows, but Expect Heightened Volatility to Persist
summary: The US stock market rallied in October, recouping some losses, and is still considered 15% undervalued by Morningstar as of October 31. Despite the recent gains, investors should prepare for continued volatility due to sluggish GDP, ongoing Fed tightening, and persistent inflation. Morningstar identifies communication services, technology, and cyclical sectors as offering the best value, while cautioning against the energy sector which is now overvalued.

title: Oracle Layoffs Hit Its Cloud Unit
summary: Oracle has reportedly laid off about 200 employees in its cloud unit, specifically within the Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) and North America Cloud Infrastructure and Technology (NACT) units. These layoffs are significant given Oracle's efforts to expand its share in the cloud market against competitors like AWS and Microsoft Azure. The company has also reportedly shifted its hiring focus away from major tech hubs to regions with lower salary expectations.

title: Perrigo buys US infant-formula brand, factory from Nestlé
summary: Perrigo has acquired the "Good Start" infant-formula brand and a manufacturing plant in Eau Claire, Wisconsin, from Nestlé. This strategic move, which includes a US$60m investment to boost capacity by 100m 8oz bottles annually, aims to address the ongoing infant formula shortage in the US and strengthen Perrigo's position as a major supplier. The company, already producing store-brand formulas for retailers like Amazon and Walmart, plans to expand its US infant formula manufacturing capabilities significantly.

title: Best Buy Co. Inc. stock underperforms Wednesday when compared to competitors
summary: Best Buy Co. Inc. (BBY) stock fell 4.17% on Wednesday, closing at $66.01, underperforming the broader market. This drop ended a three-day winning streak and left the stock $75.96 below its 52-week high. Competitors like Apple Inc. (AAPL) and Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN) also saw declines, while Walmart Inc. (WMT) experienced a lesser fall.

title: Kroger-Albertsons Merger Makes Sense Operationally
summary: The proposed merger between Kroger and Albertsons, if it closes in early 2024, would create a $200 billion company with over 5,000 stores, significantly overhauling the competitive landscape in the grocery market. Kroger CEO Rodney McMullen, referencing the successful Fred Meyer acquisition, argues the merger is necessary to better compete with larger retailers like Walmart and Amazon, allowing for cost savings, price cuts, and increased investment in digital infrastructure and retail media. The deal is expected to generate $1 billion in annual cost savings and provide greater buying power to navigate rising costs and shrinking margins in the industry.

title: Apple now valued at more than Amazon, Alphabet and Meta — combined
summary: Apple's market capitalization has surpassed the combined value of Alphabet, Amazon, and Meta Platforms, demonstrating its strong performance relative to other major technology companies this year. This achievement highlights Apple's dominant position in the tech industry, especially given that its stock has fared better than its peers.

title: Amazon commits $53 million to fast-track innovations by female climate tech entrepreneurs
summary: Amazon is investing $53 million to support female climate tech entrepreneurs and address gender inequities in climate finance. This includes $3 million for USAID's Climate Gender Equity Fund, which will provide grants and support to women-led climate solutions globally, and an additional $50 million from Amazon's Climate Pledge Fund to invest directly in women-founded and women-led climate tech companies. The initiative aims to accelerate climate innovations, advance gender equity, and enhance access to funding and technical support for women in the climate sector.

title: 'Strength in automotive' as Ansys looks to grow its simulated software solutions for vehicle makers
summary: Ansys is focusing on expanding its simulated software solutions for the automotive industry, which already represents a significant portion of its annual contract value. The company reported that its automotive customers contributed over $65 million, or 16%, to its annual contract value during the third quarter of 2022. This growth comes amidst other developments in the autonomous vehicle and tech sectors.

title: Lionsgate Takes $1.8B Hit As It Exits Seven Former Starz Markets
summary: Lionsgate incurred a $1.8 billion hit, including a $53.7 million operating loss, as it announced its exit from seven international Starz markets. This strategic decision, which includes a $1.7 billion non-cash goodwill accounting and restructuring charge, aims to stabilize the Starz business and improve profitability, potentially leading to a spinoff of its studio business. The move comes amidst ongoing strategic talks to separate its media networks and studio operations for better valuation.

title: Sprouts partners with DoorDash to expand online options
summary: Sprouts Farmers Market has partnered with DoorDash to introduce on-demand delivery services across its approximately 380 stores, starting in Phoenix and rolling out phased across other cities in November. This collaboration enhances Sprouts' existing delivery and pickup options with Instacart, making over 20,000 Sprouts products available through DoorDash's platform. Customers can choose same-day or future deliveries, and DashPass members will receive free delivery and reduced service fees.

title: Momento accelerates databases with serverless data caching
summary: Momento has launched a new serverless data caching platform designed to accelerate databases and scale database queries in the cloud more easily. The startup, which emerged from stealth mode with $15 million in seed funding, aims to help organizations, including early user CBS Sports, reduce database costs and improve performance by utilizing caching rather than directly scaling up databases. The technology is built on Twitter's open-source Pelikan caching system, optimized by Momento, and aims to enhance user interactivity in data-driven applications.

title: Shapiro files lawsuit against NY company for its alleged roll in distributing robocalls to PA consumers
summary: Pennsylvania Attorney General Josh Shapiro has filed a lawsuit against New York-based Fluent Inc. and its subsidiaries for their alleged involvement in distributing hundreds of thousands of unwanted robocalls to Pennsylvania consumers, including those on the Do Not Call List. Fluent allegedly collected personal information from consumers by promising promotional offerings and then sold this data to telemarketing companies, often without clear consent regarding telemarketing calls. The lawsuit highlights that from 2018 to 2021, over 4.2 million Pennsylvania consumers registered information on Fluent’s websites, leading to numerous violations of federal and state telemarketing laws.

title: 3 Hydrogen Stocks That Will Make You a Millionaire by 2030
summary: This article identifies three hydrogen stocks – Plug Power (PLUG), Bloom Energy (BE), and Ballard Power Systems (BLDP) – as potential millionaire-makers by 2030. It highlights hydrogen's versatility and the growing $11 trillion hydrogen economy, driven by energy and transportation needs. Each company is presented with its unique strengths, such as Plug Power's electrolyzer business and Microsoft partnership, Bloom Energy's solid-oxide fuel cells and financial targets, and Ballard Power Systems' leadership in fuel cells for heavy-duty vehicles.

title: Lambda Ephemeral Storage: Why the 10 GB Increase Is Important
summary: AWS has increased the ephemeral storage limit for Lambda functions from 512 MB to 10 GB, significantly enhancing its capability for data-intensive applications. This expansion addresses previous limitations that forced developers to use less performant workarounds like S3 or EFS for large datasets. The article discusses various use cases benefiting from this increase, such as ETL jobs, machine learning tasks, and large file processing, while also clarifying when ephemeral storage is not suitable due to its temporary nature.

title: Regeneron turns to IT to accelerate drug discovery
summary: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals is leveraging IT, particularly cloud computing and advanced data platforms, to significantly accelerate its drug discovery process. CIO Bob McCowan has spearheaded a major digital transformation, migrating the company's data to a multicloud environment (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud) and developing a MetaBio Data Discovery Platform, empowering scientists with tools to experiment and test hypotheses more efficiently. This strategic IT investment aims to reduce the drug development timeline from ten years to as few as four or five.

title: Homeland Grocery Stores name Walmart, Amazon veteran as new president and CEO
summary: HAC, Inc., parent company of Homeland Grocery Stores, has appointed David Criscione, a veteran of Walmart International, Amazon, and Delhaize Group, as its new president and CEO. Criscione will oversee 78 grocery stores in four states and replaces Marc Jones. His background includes executive roles in finance, strategy, and technology, and he was involved in Amazon's launch of physical grocery stores and the potential acquisition of Whole Foods Market.

title: An advent calendar about the hit-show "Friends" will be there for you to count down the days in December
summary: This article highlights various Advent calendars available for the 2022 holiday season, ranging from toys and tech to beauty products and gourmet treats. It emphasizes options under $50, making them budget-friendly gift ideas. Featured calendars include themes like "Friends," Disney princesses, Star Wars, Build-A-Bear, Sephora beauty, and even options for pets and escape room enthusiasts, catering to a wide audience.

title: EBay’s focus on luxury to refurbished goods drives results beat
summary: EBay Inc. surpassed Wall Street's quarterly targets as inflation-conscious shoppers increasingly bought refurbished goods and the company expanded its luxury offerings. Despite forecasting holiday-quarter revenue slightly below estimates, investors drove shares up nearly 8% in extended trading, recognizing eBay's appeal for value in a high-inflation environment. The company acknowledged risks from a strong U.S. dollar, Europe's energy crisis, and consumer confidence but noted increased demand for home energy products in Germany.

title: Amazon Continues its Cloud Expansion in Northern Virginia
summary: Amazon Web Services (AWS) is significantly expanding its data center presence in Northern Virginia by leasing large amounts of new space and increasing the size of its data centers. This expansion, primarily through its partnership with Corporate Office Properties Trust (COPT), signifies AWS's anticipation of strong future demand and its continued dominance in the cloud computing market. The article details COPT's role in building "powered shells" for Vadata (Amazon's data center operating unit) and highlights a shift towards larger data facility templates for AWS, ensuring continuous capital for COPT through joint ventures.

title: Walgreens' VillageMD inks $9B deal to buy Summit Health, marking largest physician deal of the year
summary: Walgreens' VillageMD is acquiring Summit Health, parent company of CityMD, for $8.9 billion, making it the largest physician deal of the year. This acquisition significantly expands Walgreens' reach into primary, specialty, and urgent care, creating one of the largest independent provider groups in the U.S. Cigna Corp's Evernorth is also investing and becoming a minority owner in VillageMD, aiming to enhance value-based care and integrate services.

title: EBay modernizes desktop seller tech stack, eliminates legacy tools
summary: eBay has modernized its desktop seller tech stack by migrating all desktop sellers to a single unified listing experience globally, eliminating multiple legacy tools and accelerating innovation. The company also made strategic acquisitions, including myFitment and TCGplayer, to enhance its offerings for collector items and expand its capabilities in areas like inventory management and cross-border trade. These efforts reflect a focus on improving customer experience and driving site-wide conversion, despite a slight decline in net revenue for the quarter.

title: Autonomous Delivery and Work Drones Will Still Need a Human Minder
summary: Companies are investing billions in autonomous delivery and work drones to improve efficiency and address worker shortages. However, industry executives believe that fully autonomous operation is still years away, if ever achievable, necessitating human oversight for these machines. The goal is to dramatically increase the number of machines each human operator can supervise, with companies like Serve Robotics aiming for ratios of one person to hundreds of robots to manage complex real-world situations.

title: Chaos Engineering: Unleashing havoc in production
summary: Chaos engineering, a practice pioneered by Netflix, involves intentionally disrupting production environments to identify weaknesses and build system resilience. This approach, likened to "Bootcamp for DevOps teams," helps organizations prepare for inevitable service failures in complex cloud infrastructures. Tools like Chaos Monkey and Chaos Mesh are used to simulate outages, allowing teams to develop robust systems that can recover quickly from disruptions.

title: Matter is just the first step towards the ideal smart home
summary: The Matter smart home protocol officially launched, representing a significant collaborative effort by 300 technology companies to standardize smart home device interoperability. While it aims for a seamless user experience and a revolution in product-buying, initial adoption will involve a gradual transition focusing on specific device categories like lighting, HVAC, and door locks. Future stages will incorporate more device types, but the protocol still needs to address broader issues like user data security and privacy beyond just device interoperability.

title: Jumia Technologies (JMIA) Announces Appointment of New Management Board and Acting CEO
summary: Jumia Technologies (JMIA) announced a new Management Board and the appointment of Francis Dufay as Acting CEO, with co-CEOs Jeremy Hodara and Sacha Poignonnec stepping down. The company aims to refocus on core e-commerce fundamentals, reduce operating losses, and achieve profitability. Antoine Maillet-Mezeray has been elevated to Executive Vice President, Finance & Operations, and a search for a permanent CEO is underway.

title: Jumia Tumbles as Co-Founders Step Down From African E-Commerce Platform
summary: Jumia Technologies AG co-founders Sacha Poignonnec and Jeremy Hodara have resigned from the Africa-focused online retailer, which has consistently reported losses since its New York IPO in 2019. The company, often compared to Amazon.com Inc., was founded in 2012 to bring e-commerce to African markets and attracted significant international investment, with its stock initially surging 75% on its debut.

title: Resale Shoppers to Buy More in 2023, But What About the Seller Side?
summary: A new survey by Morning Consult indicates that the robust resale market is set to grow further in 2023, with 62% of consumers having engaged in purchase-driven resale shopping and 37% expecting to increase their secondhand purchases. While buyer activity is strong across demographics, attracting sellers remains a challenge for companies like TheRealReal. The article highlights the critical imbalance between buyers and sellers, which is driving consolidation in the secondary market.

title: Gap Sells Greater China Business to Chinese E-commerce Firm for Up to $50 Million
summary: Gap is selling its Greater China business, including mainland China and Taiwan operations, to Chinese e-commerce operator Baozun for an acquisition amount of $40 million, subject to adjustments up to $50 million. The deal, expected to close in the first half of 2023, grants Baozun exclusive rights for 10 years to manage, design, manufacture, promote, and distribute Gap products in the region. This strategic move follows years of slumping sales for Gap, its exit from China with its Old Navy brand, and an intense boycott from Chinese customers over the Xinjiang cotton controversy.

title: ‘Matter’ kicks off with a bang in Amsterdam – with Silicon Labs in starring role
summary: The new 'Matter' IoT standard launched in Amsterdam, featuring Silicon Labs in a prominent role and showcasing new smart home solutions. Silicon Labs, aiming to be "the Nvidia of IoT," predicts 40 billion IoT devices by 2030 and significant growth for smart home IoT due to Matter's interoperability. The standard, backed by nearly three hundred companies, aims to simplify smart home experiences for consumers.

title: Meta Layoffs Deepen Silicon Valley’s Jobs Losses
summary: Meta Platforms announced it is laying off 13% of its workforce, over 11,000 jobs, adding to job losses across Silicon Valley's tech sector. This decision, influenced by Mark Zuckerberg's admission of misjudging pandemic-driven growth, has been praised by investors and has boosted Meta's stock. The layoffs will also severely impact H-1B visa holders and have global repercussions, particularly for Twitter's international staff.

title: The Quiet Invasion of 'Big Information'
summary: This article highlights how companies like RELX (Reed Elsevier LexisNexis) and Thomson Reuters operate largely unnoticed, despite collecting vast amounts of personal data and influencing critical life decisions. Unlike the Big Five tech companies, these "information giants" avoid public scrutiny while selling data to various institutions and privatizing public information. The author argues for robust data privacy laws, antitrust enforcement, and public funding for information access to curb their monopolistic power and prevent a digital dystopia.

title: Marketing Ethics – The Push and Pull in the digital age
summary: This article discusses the ethical challenges in digital marketing, particularly concerning data collection via voice-enabled devices and social media. Author Uma Iyer highlights how AI and machine learning are used to target consumers through their digital footprints, raising privacy concerns. The article also compares data protection laws in the US, Philippines, and EU, and examines India's evolving stance on digital privacy, emphasizing the need for robust regulations and user awareness.

title: Amazon Becomes World’s First Public Company to Lose $1 Trillion in Market Value
summary: Amazon.com Inc. has become the world's first public company to lose $1 trillion in market value, with its stock falling 4.3% on Wednesday. The e-commerce and cloud giant's value dropped to approximately $879 billion from a peak of $1.88 trillion in July 2021, attributed to rising inflation, tightening monetary policies, and disappointing earnings. Microsoft Corp. is also close to this milestone, having lost $889 billion from its November 2021 peak.

title: Innovator Equity Managed Floor ETF Holdings
summary: This article details the holdings of the Innovator Equity Managed Floor ETF (SFLR), which was established on November 9, 2022. The ETF has

title: Xperi signs second TV maker for TiVo operating system
summary: Xperi has signed Shenzhen KTC Technology as its second TV manufacturer partner for its TiVo operating system, aiming to expand its presence in the smart TV market. This announcement follows Xperi's recent disclosure of quarterly earnings and its focus on the operating side of its business rather than consumer electronics. The first TiVo OS-powered smart TV sets are expected to ship in the first half of 2023.

title: Innovator Equity Managed Floor ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NYSEARCA:SFLR) $SFLR
summary: The Innovator Equity Managed Floor ETF (SFLR) is an ETF that aims to provide capital appreciation by investing in large-cap US stocks while utilizing a laddered options strategy to hedge downside risk, targeting a maximum 10% loss on a rolling 12-month basis. Launched on November 8, 2022, the fund has $1.68 billion in assets under management and a net expense ratio of 0.89%. As of early May 2026, its stock had increased by 2.2% year-to-date and its top holdings include major tech companies like NVIDIA, Apple, and Microsoft.

title: Don't Sleep on e.l.f. Cosmetics' Magical Cyber Monday Sale
summary: e.l.f. Cosmetics is holding a Cyber Monday sale from November 29 to November 30, offering 40% off orders over $30 and a free gift for orders over $40. The article highlights several popular and affordable e.l.f. products, including the Poreless Putty Primer and Hydrating Camo Concealer. It encourages shoppers to take advantage of the sale to stock up on their favorite budget-friendly beauty items.

title: HPE SVP Hang Tan On HPE, VMware ‘Co-Innovation,’ And The $32.3B Private Cloud Opportunity
summary: HPE Senior Vice President Hang Tan discusses the new HPE GreenLake for VMware offering, emphasizing the 'massive' private cloud opportunity for partners. This collaboration integrates VMware Cloud Foundation with HPE GreenLake's consumption-based model, simplifying hybrid cloud deployments for enterprise customers. Tan highlights benefits like true consumption-based pricing, fully integrated experiences, co-innovation, and reduced complexity for channel partners, positioning HPE as a leader in the growing $32.3 billion private cloud market.

title: D-Wave reports strong revenue growth as it expands its customer base
summary: D-Wave Systems Inc., an early pioneer in quantum computing, reported strong revenue growth in its third-quarter financial results, with a 30% increase year-over-year to $1.7 million. Despite falling short of Wall Street's earnings targets with a net loss of $13 million, the company expanded its commercial customer base by 34% year-to-date and launched its Leap quantum cloud service on the Amazon Web Services marketplace. D-Wave is also progressing with its gate-model quantum machine development, aiming to address a wider range of use cases beyond its current quantum annealing technology.

title: Gap Launches Collection of Family Essentials with Amazon Fashion in U.S. and Canada
summary: Gap has launched a new collection of family essential apparel, accessories, and baby gear on Amazon Fashion in the U.S. and Canada. This collaboration aims to make Gap's modern American essentials more accessible to customers through Amazon's extensive reach and fast, free Prime delivery services. The collection includes thousands of items for adults, teens, kids, and babies, along with babyGap-branded nursery furniture.

title: Predictions 2023: Retail Health, Decentralized Trials, And Wellness Are On The Front Lines
summary: The article discusses healthcare trends for 2023, highlighting challenges like hospital bankruptcies due to economic downturns and changing consumer behaviors. It predicts a significant rise in retail health clinics' market share for primary care and increased adoption of remote patient monitoring (RPM) tools for chronic conditions. The authors emphasize the need for healthcare organizations to transform and invest in workforce talent to remain competitive.

title: DoorDash is starting to look like a tech platform
summary: DoorDash is expanding beyond its core on-demand delivery service, acquiring Wolt Enterprises Oy and Bbot, and launching "DashMart" to offer household essentials. The company is evolving into a broader tech platform by introducing self-serve ad solutions for CPG partners and a "Merchant Benefits" program that provides discounted services like healthcare and mental health benefits to its retail partners. These moves suggest DoorDash is following a path similar to Amazon or Google, differentiating itself from rivals by offering more comprehensive tech services.

title: Alibaba, JD.com keep mum on this year’s Singles’ Day transaction volume
summary: For the first time, Chinese e-commerce giants Alibaba and JD.com did not disclose their final gross merchandise volume (GMV) for the Singles' Day shopping festival, amid economic headwinds and China's zero-Covid policy. While Alibaba stated its results were in line with last year's GMV and JD.com claimed "record-breaking" results, analysts speculate the actual figures might have been underwhelming, leading to their decision to withhold specific numbers. This transparency shift reflects the challenging economic environment affecting consumer spending in China.

title: Dow pops 1,200 points, S&P 500 jumps 5% in biggest rally in two years after light inflation report
summary: Stocks experienced their largest rally since 2020 following an October consumer price index report that suggested inflation might have peaked. The Dow Jones Industrial Average surged 1,201.43 points (3.7%), the S&P 500 rose 5.54%, and the Nasdaq Composite jumped 7.35%. This market reaction was driven by a lower-than-expected CPI reading, leading traders to anticipate a less aggressive stance from the Federal Reserve regarding interest rate hikes.

title: Stove Top Launches Stuffing Pants to Help You Celebrate Thanksgiving in Comfort and Style
summary: Stove Top is bringing back its popular Stuffing Pants for its 50th anniversary to offer comfort and style for Thanksgiving celebrations. These jogger-style pants feature 360-degree stuffin’-stretch technology and an extra-wide waistband, available on Amazon.com starting November 16th for $24.90. The initiative aims to enhance the holiday experience by combining comfort with the enjoyment of Thanksgiving meals.

title: Amazon to lay off 10,000 people: Report
summary: Amazon is reportedly planning to lay off approximately 10,000 corporate and technology employees, focusing on its devices unit (including Alexa), retail division, and human resources. This move comes as the company, which recently froze corporate hiring, prepares for a potential economic downturn and slowing consumer demand, following similar job cuts by other major tech companies like Meta and Twitter.

title: Dell Drops Classical-Quantum Compute Package, Taps IonQ for Hybrid Cloud Approach
summary: Dell Technologies has launched a new hybrid classical-quantum computing package that includes a quantum emulation platform and access to IonQ’s quantum computers, enabling both on-premise and cloud-based quantum acceleration. This approach allows customers to leverage quantum technology for learning, experimentation, and eventual productization, supporting a range of use cases such as chemistry and materials simulation, machine learning, and natural language processing. Dell's strategy emphasizes the complementary roles of classical and quantum infrastructure, differing from other tech giants that develop proprietary quantum hardware.

title: Bob Greenblatt, Allison Janney Partner to Adapt ‘Confident Women’ Into Anthology Series for Amazon (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Bob Greenblatt and Allison Janney are collaborating with writer Alexa Junge to develop an anthology series called "Confident Women" for Amazon Prime Video. The series will be based on Tori Telfer's book, which explores the stories of female con women throughout history. Janney is attached as a non-writing executive producer, and each season will focus on a different woman's story, starting with Sante Kimes.

title: Build applications of any size on Cloudflare with the Queues open beta
summary: Cloudflare has launched the open beta for Cloudflare Queues, a new service designed to help developers build more complex and decoupled applications using message queues. Queues integrate with Cloudflare Workers and R2, enabling functionalities like log aggregation and efficient buffering of data before writing to storage, reducing costs and improving performance. The article details how to get started with Queues, provides a practical example of building a log sink, and outlines the underlying Cloudflare technologies used to develop the service and its future roadmap.

title: Pitney Bowes Launches PitneyShip™ Cube, the First-of-Its-Kind Shipping Label Printer With Built-In Scale
summary: Pitney Bowes has introduced PitneyShip Cube, a groundbreaking wireless shipping label printer that includes a built-in scale. This all-in-one device, combined with the PitneyShip software, enables users to streamline their shipping process by weighing packages, comparing discounted rates, printing labels, and tracking orders from a single compact unit. It is designed to benefit ecommerce sellers and office shippers by saving time and space, enhancing efficiency, and offering discounted USPS and UPS shipping rates.

title: Salesforce Accessibility Execs Derek Featherstone, Catherine Nichols Talk Disability Inside And Out Of The Company In New Interview
summary: Salesforce accessibility executives Derek Featherstone and Catherine Nichols discuss the company's commitment to disability inclusion, both internally and externally. They highlight the collaborative efforts within the tech industry to promote accessibility, the role of Salesforce's Office of Accessibility and Abilityforce ERG, and the ethical component embedded in their product development. The executives emphasize that accessibility is a continuous journey and a core value for Salesforce, aiming to create a thriving environment for disabled employees and expanding their user base globally.

title: Top 10 Oracle Competitors & Alternatives
summary: This article identifies and describes the top 10 competitors and alternatives to Oracle, a leading US-based multinational technology company providing database solutions, cloud engineering, and enterprise software products. It details each competitor's launch year, founders, headquarters, and key products/services, offering insights into the competitive landscape of the tech industry.

title: Amazon to lay off thousands of employees -source
summary: Amazon plans to lay off approximately 10,000 employees in corporate and technology roles, starting this week. This reduction, affecting about 3% of its corporate staff, includes positions in its devices organization, human resources, and retail divisions. The move is attributed to the uncertain macroeconomic environment and follows similar layoffs across the tech sector.

title: Amazon Starts Virtual Health Referral Service Linking Patients to Doctors
summary: Amazon.com Inc. has launched "Amazon Clinic," a new virtual health referral service designed to connect patients with healthcare providers for various conditions, including acne, hair loss, and allergies. This initiative marks Amazon's continued expansion into the healthcare sector, complementing its existing online pharmacy and its acquisition of One Medical. The service aims to streamline access to virtual medical consultations.

title: Record wage rises still outpaced by soaring inflation
summary: Wages in the UK are growing at their fastest rate in over 20 years, with a 5.7% increase in regular pay by September, but this growth is still severely outpaced by the soaring cost of living, which has led to a real-terms wage fall of 2.7%. The Office for National Statistics reported a slight rise in unemployment to 3.6%, though still near a 50-year low, and significant pay growth disparity between the private (6.6%) and public (2.2%) sectors, contributing to industrial tensions and recruitment challenges, particularly in public services. Chancellor Jeremy Hunt has prioritized tackling inflation ahead of his Autumn Statement, which is expected to include spending cuts, tax rises, and measures to support the poorest households.

title: Over 1,000 songs with human-mimicking AI vocals have been released by Tencent Music in China. One of them has 100m streams.
summary: Tencent Music Entertainment (TME) has released over 1,000 songs featuring human-mimicking AI vocals, with one track surpassing 100 million streams. TME used its "Lingyin Engine" to recreate the voices of late legendary artists like Teresa Teng and Anita Mui, and has also developed AI voices for active stars. Other companies like HYBE (with Supertone) and ByteDance (TikTok's parent company) are also significantly investing in AI voice synthesis and music generation.

title: The Makers Of The SPAM® Brand Celebrate The 2022 Holiday Season with Limited Edition SPAM® Figgy Pudding
summary: Hormel Foods announced the limited-edition SPAM® Figgy Pudding, a new seasonal flavor available for the 2022 holiday season. This new variety combines savory SPAM® with warm spices and seasonal ingredients, aiming to introduce consumers to the classic holiday treat. The brand also launched an animated song to reintroduce Figgy Pudding to a wider audience, following the success of past seasonal SPAM® flavors.

title: Crypto, unicorns and housing bubbles: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon talks economy in Austin
summary: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon visited Austin to discuss the economy, the implosion of FTX, and the future of banking. Dimon expressed optimism for Austin's future due to its pro-business environment and growth potential. He emphasized Texas's attractiveness for business and job creation.

title: Wayfair Still Has Its Fair Share of Issues
summary: Wayfair Inc. (NYSE: W) is struggling with significant headwinds, including a slowdown in U.S. e-commerce activity and declining customer orders, leading to its fourth consecutive quarterly loss. The company faces stiff competition from established brick-and-mortar retailers and Amazon, requiring increased marketing spend that impacts profitability. While an online shift in home goods offers long-term hope, Wayfair must reverse its revenue declines and address its growing debt to regain investor confidence.

title: Amazon Employees Fear ‘No One Is Safe’ as Layoffs Roil the Ranks
summary: Amazon employees are expressing widespread fear and dismay as the company undergoes its largest-ever round of layoffs. Many are criticizing the lack of transparency from leadership, especially CEO Andy Jassy, and uncertainty about job security is impacting productivity. The layoffs come as Amazon faces a slowing growth environment and a struggling stock performance, leading to a significant retrenchment particularly within the devices team, retail division, and human resources.

title: Lockheed Martin-Built Orion Spacecraft Launched to the Moon on Historic Artemis I Mission
summary: NASA's Artemis I mission, featuring the Lockheed Martin-built Orion spacecraft, successfully launched to the Moon, marking a significant step in human deep space exploration. The 25.5-day mission will see Orion orbit the Moon, collect data, and test new technologies like Callisto, LunIR CubeSat, and the AstroRad radiation-shielding vest before its return to Earth. This mission is a precursor to future crewed missions, aiming to land the first woman and person of color on the Moon.

title: How did department stores’ retail sales fare during Black Friday week in 2021?
summary: In 2021, consumer spending data for major department stores during Black Friday week showed mixed results. Only Dillard's retail sales reached pre-COVID levels, surpassing its 2019 figures by 1%. Kohl's recorded the highest share of its fiscal quarter sales during Black Friday week, accounting for 14% of FY21 Q4 sales.

title: Multiple firms prepare for wave of lawsuits over Huawei SEPs
summary: Huawei has initiated a wave of lawsuits in Germany against several companies, including Stellantis, Amazon, Netgear, and AVM, regarding its mobile phone and Wi-Fi 6 standard essential patents (SEPs). This marks a shift for Huawei from being predominantly a defendant to an aggressor in patent litigation. The cases, which are being handled by various law firms, highlight the increasing importance and contentious nature of SEPs in connected car and wireless technologies.

title: Violations of labor law lead to Home Depot Workers Union loss in Philly
summary: A unionization vote for the independent Home Depot Workers Union in northeast Philadelphia failed, with the union attributing the loss to rampant company labor law-breaking. The union plans to file additional charges with the NLRB, potentially seeking a rerun of the election due to alleged illegal quizzing and spying on workers by Home Depot management. This event highlights growing worker dissatisfaction in retail and warehousing over low pay and poor working conditions.

title: Mass layoffs at Amazon hit Vancouver offices
summary: Amazon's mass layoffs have extended to its Vancouver offices, as confirmed by a Vancouver-based software engineer who was among those let go. While Amazon Canada declined to provide specific numbers for Vancouver, the company indicated that general macroeconomic conditions and rapid hiring necessitated role adjustments across its global operations. This news follows a trend of significant layoffs in Vancouver's innovation sector throughout 2022.

title: Amazon lays off some devices unit staff as it targets 10,000 cuts
summary: Amazon has begun laying off employees in its devices group as part of a broader plan to cut approximately 10,000 jobs across the company, including in retail and human resources. This move comes as Amazon faces an "unusual and uncertain macroeconomic environment" and marks a significant shift for the tech giant, which has historically been known for its rapid job creation. The layoffs reflect a wider trend of dismissals within the technology sector, with other major companies like Meta Platforms and Twitter also announcing substantial job cuts.

title: eBay Inc. stock outperforms competitors despite losses on the day
summary: On Thursday, November 17, 2022, eBay Inc. stock (EBAY) fell by 0.04% to $45.47, underperforming the broader market indices like the S&P 500 and Dow Jones. Despite this daily loss, eBay outperformed competitors such as Amazon.com Inc., Walmart Inc., and Costco Wholesale Corp., which experienced larger declines. The stock closed significantly below its 52-week high, with trading volume also below its 50-day average.

title: Stock Split Watch: Is Adobe Next?
summary: This article discusses the possibility of Adobe undertaking a stock split, noting that it hasn't had one in 17 years. While splits don't change company fundamentals, they can increase retail investor interest. The author believes Adobe is a great long-term investment but doesn't anticipate a stock split happening soon, especially given current market conditions and the need for its stock price to rally above $500 to create pressure for a split.

title: Spotify rival Anghami reduces headcount by 22% as part of ‘sustained focus on profitability’
summary: Anghami, a Spotify rival focusing on the MENA region, has laid off 22% of its workforce as part of a strategic move to improve profitability amid challenging macroeconomic conditions. This reduction follows similar workforce adjustments by other music and tech companies like SoundCloud, BMI, Facebook parent Meta, and Amazon. Despite the layoffs, Anghami reported a 29% year-over-year revenue jump in Q3 to $31.7 million and a 19% reduction in cloud computing costs, reaffirming its commitment to achieving a record year in 2022.

title: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy says layoffs have already begun, and will extend into next year
summary: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy has publicly confirmed that layoffs have begun at the company and will continue into early 2023. These job cuts, potentially affecting over 10,000 workers, are primarily targeting corporate and technology roles in response to economic pressures and a period of slower growth. Jassy described the decision as difficult but expressed optimism for Amazon's future, focusing on customer obsession and innovation.

title: Broadcom’s latest switch chip offers connectivity alternative for hyperscalers
summary: Broadcom's new Tomahawk 5 switch processor aims to provide a connectivity alternative for hyperscalers by using Remote Direct Memory Access over Converged Ethernet (RoCE) to offload data movement from CPUs. This technology, along with the new Atlas2 switch based on PCIe Gen 5, targets the need for lower processing costs and higher performance in data-intensive applications. The company highlights significant savings by having the switch handle data transfer directly between servers, bypassing CPU involvement.

title: Duke Energy, Amazon strategic partnership to develop ultra-high-speed grid planning tools to aid $75B upgrade
summary: Duke Energy and Amazon Web Services have formed a three-year strategic collaboration. This partnership aims to integrate Duke-designed Intelligent Grid Services software with AWS cloud technology. The goal is to dramatically reduce grid planning analysis and processing times from weeks to minutes, supporting Duke Energy's $75 billion upgrade.

title: Sun Country CEO talks MSP airport competition, Amazon cargo flights
summary: In an interview, Sun Country Airlines CEO Jude Bricker discussed the competitive landscape at Minneapolis-St. Paul (MSP) airport, which is largely dominated by Delta Air Lines. Bricker also touched upon the expansion of Amazon cargo flights. He emphasized that customers who pay with their own money will choose Sun Country.

title: Starbucks U.S. workers at 100 stores hold one-day walkout
summary: Starbucks workers at over 100 U.S. company-owned stores staged a one-day walkout on "Red Cup Day" to protest alleged illegal retaliation against union organizing. Employees are demanding better pay, consistent schedules, and an end to actions they claim are union-busting tactics, affecting a key promotional day for the company. The walkout highlights ongoing labor disputes, with the National Labor Relations Board ordering Starbucks to rehire fired union activists and seeking injunctions against the company's interference in union elections.

title: Gap Inc. recovers in Q3 despite Yeezy debacle and heavy discounting
summary: Gap Inc. reported a Q3 recovery with net sales up 2.4% to $4.04 billion, driven by online sales and strong performance from Banana Republic. The company swung to a net income of $282 million despite writing off $53 million from the terminated Yeezy Gap collaboration and significant discounting. Analysts noted improvements but cautioned about high inventory, a late-quarter slowdown, and a downgraded holiday outlook due to market pressures.

title: Netflix Still on Top in Terms of Original Content, with 37% of All Movies and Shows
summary: A study by BB Media, commissioned by Media Play News, found that Netflix leads all streaming services in original content, offering 3,260 titles, which accounts for nearly 37% of the total original content across 41 platforms in the U.S. HBO Max and Yupp TV follow, with Amazon Prime Video ranking among the top five. When considering hours of original content, Prime Video displaces IQIYI for fourth place.

title: Network performance update: Developer Week 2022
summary: Cloudflare announced its latest network performance update during Developer Week 2022, highlighting its efforts to build the fastest network globally. Testing against competitors like Fastly's Compute@Edge and AWS Lambda@Edge, Cloudflare demonstrated superior performance across various metrics, including response times, connect times, and wait times for JavaScript and Rust functions. The company emphasizes that its optimized network infrastructure contributes to a faster developer platform, ensuring better user experiences for applications built on Cloudflare Workers.

title: Is DigitalOcean Stock a Buy Now?
summary: DigitalOcean is presented as a cloud infrastructure company targeting small businesses, developers, and startups, distinguishing itself from giants like AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud with competitive pricing. The article highlights DigitalOcean's strong financial performance in Q3, including significant revenue growth and ambitious targets for 2024, despite considerations about stock-based compensation affecting free cash flow. The author concludes that DigitalOcean is a strong buy due to its rapid growth, reasonable stock valuation, and focused niche market.

title: Costco could put delivery warehouse in Cedar Park
summary: Costco is reportedly looking to establish a new delivery warehouse in Cedar Park, a northern suburb of Austin, Texas. This move is part of the expansion of Costco Logistics, the company's division responsible for home delivery of large items, aiming to operate more like Amazon. The proposed facility would enhance Costco's national network of logistics hubs.

title: Tech forward: Beauty A.I. has inherent racial bias—but it doesn't have to
summary: Joy Buolamwini's experience at MIT revealed inherent racial bias in AI facial recognition, performing poorly on darker skin. Her research, echoed by Dr. Ellis Monk, links this to non-diverse training data and colorism in society. Google's partnership with Dr. Monk to implement the inclusive Monk Skin Tone Scale and Perfect Corp.'s proactive approach show how the industry is addressing and working to correct these biases for more inclusive AI.

title: I Love My Peloton. Cry Me A River.
summary: The author enthusiastically shares her positive experience with the Peloton Bike+, highlighting its diverse workout options, quiet operation, and ability to make exercise enjoyable and consistent. She details the features that make it a smart investment despite the cost, such as the rotating screen, adjustable sound, and wide range of live and on-demand classes. While acknowledging the subscription cost, she concludes that her Peloton has been a valuable investment in her health and well-being.

title: Outlook 2023: Digital Twins Will No Longer Be an Option
summary: Digital twins are rapidly evolving beyond their initial applications in discrete industrial products to encompass a wide range of industries and tasks, such as supply chains, healthcare, autonomous vehicles, and banking. This expansion is driven by their ability to generate insights, automate processes, and monitor assets, making them a strategic element of digital transformation. The article highlights the increasing complexity, the formation of new partnerships among solution providers, and the emergence of industry standards groups, emphasizing that digital twins will become an indispensable tool.

title: Tech firms pitch anti-Elon Musk management style in bid to woo former Twitter staff
summary: Following widespread layoffs and resignations at Twitter under Elon Musk's new ownership, several tech companies are actively recruiting former Twitter employees by critiquing Musk's management style. Companies like HubSpot, CoderPad, and Calix are emphasizing more employee-friendly cultures, remote work options, and opportunities for dissent to attract skilled tech talent. This recruitment drive highlights the high demand for experienced digital workers despite broader tech industry layoffs.

title: Inflation Drives Holiday Bargain Hunt
summary: A Morgan Stanley Research survey indicates that holiday shoppers are greatly influenced by inflation, leading 70% to wait for discounts before purchasing. Consumers are prioritizing experiences like travel over big-ticket items such as electronics and luxury goods. Retailers are expected to offer competitive prices due to oversupply, potentially impacting their profit margins.

title: HP says it will cut workforce by 4,000-6,000 by end of fiscal 2025
summary: HP Inc. announced plans to reduce its global workforce by 4,000 to 6,000 employees by the end of fiscal year 2025 as part of its "Future Ready Transformation" plan. This move is expected to incur approximately $700 million in labor costs. The computer manufacturer cited a challenging fourth quarter with net revenue down to $14.8 billion from $16.68 billion the previous year, and a 13% decrease in its personal systems segment.

title: These 2 ETFs show why owning small-cap stocks is key to beating the market at times like this
summary: Small-cap stocks within the S&P 500 have significantly outperformed larger-cap stocks this year, with the eight largest market cap stocks experiencing an average loss of 40.4% compared to a 9.5% average loss for the remaining stocks. This highlights how an equal-weight strategy can be more beneficial for S&P 500 investors when the biggest names are struggling. The article suggests that owning small-cap stocks is crucial for beating the market in such conditions.

title: Amazon Plans to Invest $1 Billion a Year in Movies for Theaters
summary: Amazon plans to invest over $1 billion annually to produce 12 to 15 movies for theatrical release, marking its largest commitment to cinemas. This strategy aims to compete with major studios like Paramount Pictures, with a gradual increase in film output starting next year. The move signifies a significant expansion of Amazon's presence in the film distribution market.

title: NASDAQ Trading - How to invest in NASDAQ (US100) index?
summary: This article provides a comprehensive guide on investing in the NASDAQ (US100) index, detailing its structure, how it works, and reasons for its high volatility. It explains different trading positions (long and short) and identifies opportune times for trading, such as during periods of market panic or significant company announcements. The article also touches upon the use of CFDs and ETFs for investing in NASDAQ.

title: Outer Banks vacation-themed television channel OBXVacay launches on Roku, Amazon FireTV
summary: OBXVacay, a new television channel focused on the Outer Banks of North Carolina, has launched as a free app on Roku and Amazon FireTV platforms. The channel offers 24/7 programming, including locally produced content about the region's attractions, history, and events, as well as classic shows. It aims to provide viewers with information for trip planning, during their stay, or for a virtual getaway.

title: Amazon acquires two data centers from State Street Corp in Massachusetts
summary: Amazon has acquired two data centers in Massachusetts from State Street Corp for a total of $26.7 million. The properties, located in Grafton and Westborough, include existing data center facilities and greenfield land. This acquisition suggests Amazon might demolish and rebuild the sites as part of its data center expansion, despite not having an AWS cloud region in Massachusetts.

title: Black Friday 2022: From Target and Walmart to Best Buy and Apple - deals for holiday shopping
summary: This article provides a comprehensive guide to Black Friday 2022 deals from numerous major retailers including Target, Walmart, Amazon, Best Buy, and Apple, covering various categories such as tech, home goods, clothing, and cosmetics. It highlights specific offers and sale dates for each retailer. The piece also includes expert tips on how to effectively navigate Black Friday sales to ensure shoppers get the best value for their money.

title: How to Back Up S3 Data using AWS Backup
summary: This article explains how to back up S3 data using AWS Backup, highlighting its features such as automated scheduling, incremental backups, and encryption. It provides a step-by-step guide for creating an on-demand backup of an S3 bucket via the AWS console and discusses the current limitations of AWS Backup for S3. The author also briefly mentions NetApp BlueXP as an alternative solution for NetApp Cloud Volumes deployments.

title: Dimensional U.S. Core Equity 2 ETF DFAC
summary: This article provides details on the Dimensional U.S. Core Equity 2 ETF (DFAC), including its current price, key metrics, and how to invest in it through eToro. DFAC aims to replicate the performance of the Russell 3000 Index and holds investments in over 2,500 US companies across various sectors, with major holdings like Apple and Microsoft. The ETF, established in 2007 by Dimensional Fund Advisors, had net assets of $14.7 billion as of September 2022.

title: Employers Rethink Need for College Degrees in Tight Labor Market
summary: A tight labor market is leading more employers, including Google, Delta Air Lines, and IBM, to reduce college degree requirements for certain positions, focusing instead on skills and experience. This trend has resulted in a decline in job postings requiring bachelor's degrees compared to pre-pandemic levels. The shift is influenced by high demand for workers, low unemployment, and efforts to address racial disparities in the workplace.

title: Sonos speakers almost never go on sale, but they're 20% off for Cyber Monday
summary: Sonos speakers are rarely discounted, but several models are currently 20% off at Crutchfield for Cyber Monday. The article highlights deals on popular Sonos products like the Sonos One (Gen 2), Sonos Move, Sonos Beam (Gen 2), and Sonos Arc, noting their quality and the uncommon opportunity to purchase them at a reduced price. The author, a long-time Sonos user, highly recommends these products for their reliability and sound performance.

title: JCPenney was once a shopping giant. Can it make a comeback?
summary: JCPenney's new CEO, Marc Rosen, is attempting to revitalize the 120-year-old brand by appealing to "America's diverse working families" with an overhauled beauty strategy, remodeled stores, and improved online experience. Despite a strong start to the holiday season, the company faces challenges from inflation, intense competition, and a need to attract new, younger customers. JCPenney, which filed for bankruptcy in 2020 and is now owned by mall landlords, aims to leverage its reduced debt and strategic focus on its core customer base to secure its future in a challenging retail landscape.

title: House Republicans target U.S. Chamber of Commerce as GOP battle against ‘woke capitalism’ revs up
summary: House Republicans are intensifying their campaign against "woke capitalism," targeting corporations that have embraced environmental, social, and governance (ESG) goals or supported Democratic candidates. This has put the U.S. Chamber of Commerce in the crosshairs, with House Speaker Kevin McCarthy reportedly pushing for a leadership change after the Chamber endorsed some Democrats. The growing rift between the GOP and big business stems from differing views on social issues, immigration, and climate change, threatening legislative gridlock and increasing scrutiny on corporate practices.

title: BlackBerry makes its QNX operating system available on AWS
summary: BlackBerry has announced the availability of its QNX operating system on Amazon Web Services (AWS) cloud platform at AWS re:Invent 2022. QNX, a real-time operating system used in over 215 million vehicles globally, will enable automakers to develop and test new vehicle software more efficiently in the cloud using Amazon EC2 instances. This move also extends QNX's potential use to other industries like robotics, medical equipment, and aerospace.

title: "Twelve Days of Christmas" - 12 companies for the Santa Claus Rally
summary: This article discusses the "Santa Claus Rally," a stock market phenomenon typically occurring in late December and early January, where the S&P 500 historically sees an average rise of 1.3%. It examines past rallies, their occurrence during bear markets, and potential reasons for the phenomenon, such as tax optimization and investor sentiment. The article then highlights 12 companies, including Amazon, Alphabet, and NVIDIA, that could benefit from this rally and provide investment opportunities based on their current valuations and market positions.

title: New Renderings Provide Detailed Look at 630-Unit Development at Americana Hotel Site in Crystal City
summary: New renderings offer a detailed view of the planned 636-unit residential development at the former Americana Hotel site in Crystal City, Arlington. JBG Smith's project at 1400 Richmond Highway will feature a 19-story building with retail space and extensive parking, designed by bKL Architecture. The development is situated adjacent to Amazon's HQ2, with site challenges noted due to its sloping nature and surrounding properties.

title: Cyber Monday TV & Sonos deals: save up to $2,000 instantly
summary: This article highlights Cyber Monday deals on televisions and Sonos speakers, with savings of up to $2,000 on TVs and up to 20% off Sonos products. It details specific discounts on various models from brands like Samsung, LG, Sony, and Sonos, alongside mentioning other tech sales for Apple products. The deals were available on Cyber Monday 2022 and included popular items like The Frame TVs, OLED TVs, and various Sonos soundbars and speakers.

title: Tenneco to Supply Solutions for Rivian R1T and R1S EVs
summary: Tenneco has been selected to provide intelligent suspension and anti-vibration materials for Rivian's R1T pickup and R1S SUV electric vehicles. The Rivian models will feature Tenneco's Monroe Intelligent Suspension CVSA2/Kinetic H2 semi-active suspension technology and Clevite Elastomers NVH performance materials. This technology, originally for sport and hypercars, offers advanced hydraulic roll control, continuously controlled damping, and helps reduce vehicle weight by eliminating conventional sway bars, thus extending battery range.

title: After yearslong pause, 208-apartment complex near Micron site is moving ahead
summary: A 208-unit apartment complex, Tocco Villaggio III, which has been on hold for eight years, is now proceeding near the future Micron Technology Inc. chip factory in Clay, New York. Homebuilders Joseph E. Alberici and Joseph G. Alberici plan to construct the $57 million complex, consisting of eight buildings with one- and two-bedroom apartments, with an aim to complete it within two years. The developers are seeking $3 million in tax abatements to accelerate construction, citing rising costs and the anticipated demand for housing from the Micron plant and a new Amazon distribution center.

title: Kohl’s sets pay for interim CEO Thomas Kingsbury
summary: Kohl's has set the compensation for Thomas Kingsbury, who will serve as interim chief executive officer while the company searches for a permanent successor to Michelle Gass. Kingsbury was chosen to lead the business during this transitional period. The announcement was made in late November 2022.

title: American Eagle CEO Says Company ‘Plays by the Rules’
summary: American Eagle Outfitters Inc. reported a solid bottom-line profit in the third quarter despite a revenue dip and decreasing gross margins. CEO Jay Schottenstein emphasized that the company "plays by the rules" regarding sourcing and manufacturing and expects competitors to do the same. The company is actively managing inventory, expecting further reductions, and focusing on strategic initiatives and innovations, including expanding Aerie and launching a new men’s subbrand, to drive future growth.

title: Where Does All the Cardboard Come From? I Had to Know. (Published 2022)
summary: This article delves into the massive and rapidly growing cardboard industry, tracing the journey of a cardboard box from a loblolly pine tree to a finished product. It highlights the dominance of major companies like International Paper, the environmental benefits of cardboard's recyclability compared to other materials, and how e-commerce has fueled an unprecedented demand for packaging. The piece also touches on innovations in packaging and global market dynamics, including China's role as a major consumer and the industry's significant impact on regional economies.

title: Fubo Sports Network Now Streaming on Amazon Freevee
summary: Fubo Sports Network, the ad-supported TV network from FuboTV, has launched on Amazon Freevee, expanding its reach to over 155 million devices across various streaming platforms. The network, which reported its highest viewership in September 2022, now features original programming like “Airing It Out” with Housh and Scandrick and “The Young Person Basketball Podcast” with R.J. Hampton. This launch aims to provide more athlete-driven content to a broader audience at no additional cost.

title: Amazon Launches Supply-Chain Software Service
summary: Amazon.com Inc. has introduced "AWS Supply Chain," a new cloud-based software service designed to help businesses manage and track cargo flows. This move positions Amazon as a competitor to existing supply-chain software providers such as Manhattan Associates and Blue Yonder, and follows a similar launch by Microsoft Corp. The service aims to assist businesses, especially the numerous small and medium-sized businesses in Amazon's marketplace, in gaining better control over their complex supply chains.

title: Sonos One vs One SL: are the extra features worth the price difference? I own both, here's what I think...
summary: This article compares the Sonos One and Sonos One SL speakers, highlighting that their primary difference is the built-in smart assistant (Alexa or Google Assistant) in the Sonos One, which the One SL lacks. The author, who owns both, notes that both speakers offer identical, high-quality sound and are visually similar, with only a $20 price difference. The recommendation is to opt for the One SL if you're building a stereo pair and already have a smart speaker, or if you don't need voice assistant features, otherwise the Sonos One generally offers better value for the small price increase.

title: Amazon pays $26.7 million for properties in Grafton, Shrewsbury and Westborough
summary: Amazon Data Services Inc. has purchased properties in Grafton, Shrewsbury, and Westborough, Massachusetts, for a total of $26.7 million from State Street Corp. These acquisitions include a 1.8-acre property in Grafton for $15.1 million and properties at 600 and 800 Friberg Parkway in Westborough for $11.6 million. Amazon has not yet disclosed its development plans for these newly acquired sites to the respective towns, though it recently bought a 93-acre lot in Westborough for a delivery station.

title: Customer impacts of Kroger, Albertsons merger could depend on market, expert says
summary: The proposed merger between grocery giants Kroger and Albertsons, valued at $24.6 billion, is expected to significantly impact consumers. While the companies claim the merger will lead to lower prices and increased investment in stores and wages, an expert suggests that customer impacts will largely depend on market concentration. In highly concentrated markets, price increases are possible, whereas less concentrated markets might see price decreases.

title: Fubo Sports Network Now Available on Amazon Freevee
summary: Fubo Sports Network, FuboTV's free-to-consumer TV network, has expanded its distribution by launching on Amazon Freevee, making its content available on over 155 million devices. The network offers live sports, original programming, and partner content, with recent viewership increasing by 121% year-over-year. This expansion aims to connect with a wider audience and enhance accessibility to athlete-driven content at no additional cost.

title: Exclusive Q&A: MongoDB CEO Dev Ittycheria on empowering developers and how AWS is changing
summary: MongoDB CEO Dev Ittycheria discusses the company's strong partnership with AWS and its unique document-based data structure that empowers developers. He highlights how MongoDB's platform provides a unified and elegant user experience, enabling rapid innovation for a diverse customer base. Ittycheria also shares his insights on the evolving cloud landscape, the importance of developer productivity, and the shift towards smart applications leveraging AI and machine learning.

title: Amazon Launches Supply-Chain Software Service
summary: Amazon Web Services has launched a new supply-chain software service, entering the burgeoning tech sector that aims to bring more efficiency and visibility to goods management. This move positions Amazon alongside established players like Blue Yonder and SAP, as well as other big operators such as Microsoft, in helping businesses navigate supply chain disruptions. The service is expected to find a ready audience among the thousands of small- and medium-sized businesses on Amazon's third-party marketplace.
